from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Ternary Bridge", [
            "Ternary systems use three digits: zero, one, two.", 
            "Each digit represents a unique branching path state.", 
            "These represent transitions between three logical pegs."
        ])
        
        c0 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=0.6)
        c1 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.6)
        c2 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#3357FF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        
        l0 = Text("0", font_size=24).move_to(c0.get_center())
        l1 = Text("1", font_size=24).move_to(c1.get_center())
        l2 = Text("2", font_size=24).move_to(c2.get_center())
        
        node0 = VGroup(c0, l0)
        node1 = VGroup(c1, l1)
        node2 = VGroup(c2, l2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"), run_time=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(node0, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(node1, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(node2, "B6")
        self.play(FadeIn(node0), FadeIn(node1), FadeIn(node2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"), run_time=0.5)
        path = CurvedArrow(node0.get_center(), node1.get_center(), angle=-TAU/6)
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.play(FadeOut(path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"), run_time=0.5)
        # Visualizing transitions
        self.play(node0.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"]), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(node1.animate.move_to(self.grid["D4"]), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(node2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"]), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We add a strict adjacent move constraint.",
            "Disks move only to immediate neighboring pegs.",
            "Three disks require three-cubed minus one steps."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Constrained Towers of Hanoi", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual assets
        towers = VGroup(*[Line(UP, DOWN).set_color(YELLOW) for _ in range(3)])
        # Positioning towers at B2, B4, B6 is too cramped, let's use area
        self.place_at_grid(towers[0], 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(towers[1], 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(towers[2], 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        disks = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(height=0.2, width=w, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=1)
            for w in [1.5, 1.2, 0.9]
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Create(towers))
        for i, disk in enumerate(disks):
            disk.next_to(towers[0], DOWN, buff=-0.2 - i*0.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(disks))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        formula = MathTex("3^3 - 1 = 26", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Moves to the Sierpinski Triangle", [
            "- Legal moves trace a Sierpinski triangle path.",
            "- Each fractal level mirrors the state space.",
            "- The disk path creates a beautiful geometric fractal."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # 1. Fade in the text 'Sierpinski Mapping'
        mapping_text = Text("Sierpinski Mapping", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(mapping_text, 'A3')
        self.play(FadeIn(mapping_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # 2. Draw the base triangle with Sierpinski pattern
        def get_sierpinski(order, length):
            if order == 0:
                return Triangle(color="#00FFFF").scale_to_fit_width(length)
            
            sub_triangle = get_sierpinski(order - 1, length / 2)
            
            # Arrange 3 sub-triangles
            t1 = sub_triangle.copy()
            t2 = sub_triangle.copy()
            t3 = sub_triangle.copy()
            
            # Position manually (basic layout)
            t1.shift(UP * (length/4) * np.sqrt(3))
            t2.shift(LEFT * (length/2) + DOWN * (length/4) * np.sqrt(3))
            t3.shift(RIGHT * (length/2) + DOWN * (length/4) * np.sqrt(3))
            
            return VGroup(t1, t2, t3)

        sierpinski = get_sierpinski(2, 2.0)
        self.place_in_area(sierpinski, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(sierpinski))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # 3. Map tower moves onto triangle fractal transitions
        path = VMobject(color=ORANGE, stroke_width=3)
        # Simplified path representing Hanoi move sequence
        points = [sierpinski[0].get_center(), sierpinski[1].get_center(), sierpinski[2].get_center(), sierpinski[0].get_center()]
        path.set_points_smoothly(points)
        
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=2)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Unified Synthesis & Conclusion", [
            "Ternary logic, constraints, and fractals are isomorphic.",
            "The Hanoi tower path forms a Sierpinski triangle.",
            "Geometry reveals hidden mathematical structural symmetries.",
            "Counting is simply navigating this unified fractal space.",
            "All complex systems share these fundamental hidden patterns."
        ])
        
        # 1. Fade in the text 'Synthesis'. (#FFFFFF)
        synthesis_text = Text("Synthesis", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(synthesis_text, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(synthesis_text))

        # 2. Overlay ternary, Hanoi, and Sierpinski visuals.
        # Represented by simple geometric shapes
        ternary_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE)
        hanoi_rect = Rectangle(height=0.8, width=0.8, color=GREEN)
        sierpinski_tri = Triangle(color=YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(ternary_circle, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(hanoi_rect, 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(sierpinski_tri, 'D4')
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(ternary_circle),
            FadeIn(hanoi_rect),
            FadeIn(sierpinski_tri),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )

        # 3. Highlight their structural equivalence using connecting lines. (#FF0000)
        line1 = Line(ternary_circle.get_center(), hanoi_rect.get_center(), color=RED)
        line2 = Line(hanoi_rect.get_center(), sierpinski_tri.get_center(), color=RED)
        
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Hidden Geometry of Counting: From Ternary Logic to Sierpinski Fractals
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: The Ternary Bridge (Prerequisite Concept)
sections.content: Introduce the base-3 (ternary) numbering system as the foundation. Contrast it with binary to explain how ternary 'digits' (0, 1, 2) naturally represent three-way branching paths or three-peg systems.
sections.example: A smart lock that requires a 3-digit ternary code to open, visualizing the sequence 0-1-2 as transitions between states.

sections.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Introduce the 'Adjacent-Only' constraint: disks can only move to an adjacent peg. Explain how this restriction forces a sequence of moves that mimics a recursive pattern, mapping directly to ternary counting.
sections.example: A robot arm restricted to moving a disk only to the immediate left or right peg; show that moving a 3-disk tower requires exactly 3^n - 1 steps.

sections.title: Mapping Moves to the Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Visually map the sequence of legal moves in the constrained Hanoi puzzle onto the edges of a Sierpinski triangle. Each level of the triangle represents the state space of the disks.
sections.example: An animation of a disk-moving path that traces the perimeter of a growing Sierpinski fractal as the number of disks increases.

sections.title: Unified Synthesis & Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize how the ternary representation, the movement constraints, and the fractal geometry are isomorphic. The 'state' of the tower is simply a coordinate in a 2D fractal space.
sections.example: A final visual showing the 'Hanoi path' drawing the Sierpinski triangle in real-time, demonstrating that mathematics is just the discovery of these hidden structural symmetries.
